# FACTS — the index of what is already established

**GENERATED by `tools/build_facts.py` from `LESSONS.md` and `STATE.md`.**
Do not edit by hand — edit the source and regenerate. 1086 facts.

## Use this BEFORE deriving anything

```
grep -i <keyword> FACTS.md          # does the record already answer this?
```

Each line ends with the `file:line` that carries the measurement. Read that
entry before re-deriving its subject.

**Two rules this file exists to enforce:**

1. **For a question about a FEATURE, read the file that implements it first.**
   A block list, a flag, a tool's tables — the answer is usually a code
   comment, not a derivation. (2026-09-24: a 60-line analysis of the WRAMCODE
   block set was committed 22 minutes after the builder committed the block
   list itself, comment and all.)

2. **Never assert a negative about the record without grepping it in the same
   turn.** "Never measured", "not reported", "no instrument exists" — each of
   those was wrong at least once, and each cost a correction round-trip.

The game's text writers mark the 4-row group they write (patch_game.py TXTMASK, WRAM byte 0xFFA1A6); the shim posts the mask in COMM2's high byte (the master reads only bits 0-2 of COMM2 for the bank) and clears it once the master has captured; every 8th vint the mask is forced full so an ungated writer is never stale for more than 8 vints. The master's inline capture copies only the marked groups: ~14 text writes a vint touch 1-2 groups of 128 longs instead of 928. On the FPGA the full capture was the largest term past the guard (144)  `Makefile:810`

The new word has one writer, is tagged, and an untagged read means FULL capture -- the failure direction is slow-and-right, never fast-and-wrong. Barcode bytes 3 and 4 are reserved for it (5 and 6 are PORTTEST's). Never a ship  `Makefile:3398`

- TCPAGE=n: which CATEGORY page the suite opens on (0 CORE, 1 68K TIMING, 2 Z80 BUS, 3 32X VDP). The pad pages between them, but the MiSTer rig takes no pad input over the launch API -- only screenshots come back -- so a page past the first is unreachable there without this. One rom per page is the whole cost of capturing the FPGA's answer for every category  `Makefile:3439`
- RIGRATE=1 (2026-09-26): THE WHOLE-RUN CADENCE RATE on the barcode. byte 5 = game frames per vint x 255 accumulated since boot (255 = 60 Hz, 128 = every other vint), byte 6 = vints/256 so the reader can see it has settled. Every other rig speed reading is a per-step accumulator sampled once or twice a launch, which is why the ~15-line per-launch spread keeps swamping the thing being measured; this one CONVERGES, so four launches give four numbers. Needs RIGBARCODE=1. Overrides bytes 5/6, so it excludes the RIGSPAN modes  `Makefile:3451`
- SH2BENCH=1 (2026-09-25): SH-2 CYCLES PER INSTRUCTION, on the rig. Two loops with exactly known instruction counts (register-ALU cache-resident, and cached SDRAM loads at a 128-byte stride) timed with the master's FRT, published as cycles/instr x 8 on the 9-bit value channel, variant in bits 8-7. Read with tools/rig_value.py -n 16 --layout trip PORT-CENSUS.md's 7-19x port ratio rests on this number being 1.5-4.0 and it has never been measured -- ares charges instruction count only. Destroys the picture (it floods CRAM every vint); it is a probe, never a shipping flag  `Makefile:3462`

The game runs to our presentation clock instead of racing the beam  `Makefile:3625`

- DIRECTFB=1 = REBUILD stage 1 (2026-08-26, the FBBENCH verdict): every compose writer's dst row moves from sbuf to the FB BACK BANK directly (cached window; FB writes cost the same as SDRAM writes, 0.99x). The clears become FB-row long-fills (the FB IGNORES ZERO BYTE writes — a byte clear would be a no-op), blit_half's row loop is inert (the machinery stays wired; it dies whole in stage 2), and the k2 flip is gated on "this interval actually composed" so an AUTO-30 launch skip HOLDS the frame instead of stepping the display backward two frames. WHICH BANK needs no plumbing: 0x04000000 maps the DRAW bank by hardware and the whole compose interval sits between k2 flips  `Makefile:3652`

Four variants measured 2026-08-25 (raw, DREQ-park, window-park, COMM0-yield, FM-park): ALL bracket rejects 10-14% vs the master-chain's 2.0 — the slave's frame-body idle is LOAD-BEARING bus quiet, and parking enough to protect it refunds the latency win (skipped back to 47%+). DO NOT re-try a fifth park shape; the next real lever is shrinking compose itself (§11 pack, MD text). Default = master-relaunched chain with the bounded hold  `Makefile:3703`
- NATIVE=1 = the whole-frame pipeline (branch native1, docs/design/NATIVE.md, 2026-08-31 — Mike's "gates should be for an entire screen update"). ONE generation in flight and it is the WHOLE frame: launch latches regs+records once, the slave composes all three bands from one self-chain command with cat1+text inline, the master tail (text halves + build_maps) runs as poll-gap chunks, the blit ships ONLY closed generations and the ISR flips ONLY freshly-blitted banks. Band queue / chain relaunch / ROW_DEFER / cat1 deferral compile out. 60Hz when a generation closes in a vint; whole-frame-coherent 30Hz when it does not — never a band, never a mixed frame. NOT the SELFCHAIN experiment (which kept per-band ships racing the compose); see docs/design/NATIVE.md's ledger notes before citing that negative  `Makefile:3716`

Counts, per run: vints in the normal scene vs any other, times the glow animator YIELDED to the 68K (the transform gate), vints a mask grant sat undelivered because COMM8 was busy, the longest such run, and vints the animator actually ticked. Answers whether Mike's flat chevron is the animator yielding and the 68K never being told to stop masking those blocks  `Makefile:3763`
- GLOWRATE=1 = NOTES 67 / LOOP29 276. Per 64 vints, the number of vints in which the chevron/glow ramp (PAL_SH 0x98-0x9F, set 19) CHANGED. The rig's only instrument is the value channel and its screenshot path samples at ~0.5 Hz, far too slow to see a per-vint rotation directly. Pair it with NOGLOW=1 to measure the DELTA PATH's ability to animate those words -- the state the SH-2 animator hands them to in the transform scene, which the attract never reaches. NEEDS BOOTFLIPRATE: the CRAM flood that makes the value channel readable lives under BOOT_VALUE, and BOOT_FLIPRATE is what selects 0xFFA18A as its source. GLOW_RATE's write runs AFTER the flip-rate write in the same vint, so it wins the word and the flood shows the ramp count. Built without it, the probe writes a word nothing paints and every capture reads "unreadable" -- which is what the first cut did (LOOP29 276)  `Makefile:3769`

The compare is given the same TAPE the port replayed; section 0 of the report refuses a corpus recorded on another tape or on other DIPs than the port boots with  `Makefile:4294`
- SWEEP=1 adds the full sweep after the gate: every arcade tick of both demos, all 64 records live or dead plus the globals (tests/demo-b/sweep_demo.py). ~25 minutes  `Makefile:4330`
- PORTTAPEPAD=<tape.csv> PORTTAPEARCADE=<arcade corpus dir> = MEASUREMENT ONLY: the input tape compiled into the rom and applied by game frame at each tick (sh_src/port_l2.c l2m_io_tape), because ares injects input per wall frame and lands it 0-1 game frames late. Needs R60LIVEPAD (the port's pad cells) and the tick-end counter; parity_play --rom-tape  `Makefile:5049`
- FFFFF400=4 REMOVED 2026-10-04: the 68K reads and increments 0xFFF400 as a BYTE (0x3B44 moveb, 0x3B4E addqb) -- the palette-slot counter -- and only the 8-byte INIT at 0x3B10 writes it as part of a long. With the cell forced to 4 bytes the compare `DAT_fffff400 < 0x3f` read the counter | 0xFFF401 | the queue pointer's high word and never allocated a sprite-palette slot: PAL_SH sets 64-79 absent in every port build (rd9-rd12). The init copy is rewritten by cport_prep.py instead  `Makefile:5300`
- FFFFD400=2 (2026-10-04): the slot-40 object's flag is a WORD (`movew #0x8000,(fp)` at 0x16B6E with fp = 0xFFD400); as a uint the store put 00 00 80 00 and the slot never activated (arcade f947: slot 40 active with handler 0x16BF0; port: flag 0)  `Makefile:5306`
- FFFFD580=2 (2026-10-25): slot 43's flag is a WORD, both writers say so: `movew #0x8000,%a0@(0)` at 0x56C6 (a0 = 0xFFD580, the intro's typewriter object, handler 0x56E8) and `movew #0x8000, %fp@(0)` at 0x18A00 (fp = 0xFFD580, the fourth record 0x1892A spawns). Ghidra typed it uint, so the store put 00 00 80 00 and the handler's long at +2 then overwrote the 0x8000: the slot never went live, and "I COMMAND YOU TO RISE FROM YOUR GRAVE" was never typed (sw318, text rows 9/11 zero through the whole intro; the arcade's 0xFFD580 reads 8000 56E8 from frame 1060). GHIDRA'S uRam/cRam/bRam NAMES (an access it resolved through a register-held base, so no absolute operand exists for the census) default to `uint` in dat_syms.h. The real width is the instruction's: measured 2026-10-04, `uRamffffdfa1 = 2` (0xF27A move.b #2,0x21(a5)) stored a 32-bit 2 over slot 63's +0x21..+0x24, so the record started at anim index 0 with state 2. Every WORK-RAM uRam cell below was read from its instruction (tools/cport_widths.py cannot see them): 0xFFC460-6/0xFFC4E0-6 = 0xF494../0xD618.. move.w (player 2's box words); 0xFFC48B 0x5430 move.b; 0xFFC4A0 0xD644 move.b; 0xFFD48A-0xFFD64E 0x17FE2.. move.b (palette copies, +0xb, +0x4e); 0xFFD822 0x5ED8 move.w; 0xFFD900 0x5EE6 clr.w; 0xFFDE80/0xFFDEC0/0xFFDEC4 0x58E4/0x58F8/0x58FE move.w; 0xFFDE89/8B/A1/A2/AF 0x58F2..0x5914 move.b/clr.b; 0xFFDF21/0xFFDFA1 0xF256/0xF27A clr.b/move.b; 0xFFFC82/83 0x42B4/0x42BA move.b. 0x19846/0x19850 (2026-10-28): level-four boss velocity/acceleration constants are MOVE.W via A0 at 0x1925A/0x19264/0x1935E. Byte declarations read 0x01/0x00 instead of 0x0100/0x0004, so the vertical orbit never reverses  `Makefile:5309`
